prompt.context_jp: 隣を歩く男は歩幅を合わせ、荷物を持つ手にも余分な力みがない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 隣を歩く男___歩幅を合わせ、荷物を持つ手にも余分な力みがない。

feedback.correct_en: The narrator has already established Nagisa as the subject of this passage; は marks him as the ongoing topic whose actions are being described.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce him as new information, but Nagisa is already the known referent walking beside Mei.

contrast_examples.en: The man walking beside me is quiet. (topic)

contrast_examples.jp: 隣を歩く男が急に話しかけてきた。
contrast_examples.en: The man walking beside me suddenly spoke up. (new event)

prompt.context_jp: うららかな朝の光が中庭のタイルに落ち、季節外れの蝶がふらりと横切っていく。
prompt.prompt_jp: うららかな朝の光が中庭のタイルに落ち、季節外れの蝶___ふらりと横切っていく。

feedback.correct_en: The butterfly is newly introduced into the scene — が presents it as a fresh element appearing in view.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the butterfly was an already-known topic, but it just appears into the morning light.

prompt.context_jp: メイの胸には、これまでの慌ただしい日々とは違う、妙に落ち着いた高揚があった。
prompt.prompt_jp: メイの胸には、これまでの慌ただしい日々とは違う、妙に落ち着いた高揚___あった。

feedback.correct_en: The exhilaration is newly introduced as the thing that exists in her chest — が marks this new existence.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presume the feeling was already a known topic, but it is being described for the first time.

contrast_examples.en: There was exhilaration in her chest.

contrast_examples.jp: その高揚は長く続いた。

prompt.context_jp: 顔だけは涼しく、内心は冷や汗まみれだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 顔だけ___涼しく、内心は冷や汗まみれだった。

feedback.correct_en: This is a contrastive は: 'as for the face' versus 'as for the inside.' The parallel structure with 内心は demands は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark new-information subject and lose the deliberate contrast between outer appearance and inner state.

contrast_examples.jp: 顔は笑っているが、心は泣いている。
contrast_examples.en: The face is smiling, but the heart is crying. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 朝の住宅街は通勤の人影がまばらで、足音が思ったより大きく響く。
prompt.prompt_jp: 朝の住宅街は通勤の人影がまばらで、足音___思ったより大きく響く。

feedback.correct_en: The topic is 朝の住宅街; within that frame, 足音 is newly described as echoing. が marks this descriptive subject inside the topic frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would create a second competing topic and break the single-topic structure.

contrast_examples.jp: 街は静かで、鳥の声がよく聞こえる。
contrast_examples.en: The town is quiet, and birdsong is clearly heard.

prompt.context_jp: メイは心の中で、こんなウソつきな自分を静かに詫びた。
prompt.prompt_jp: メイ___心の中で、こんなウソつきな自分を静かに詫びた。

feedback.correct_en: Mei is the established protagonist and the topic of this narrative passage; は marks her as the ongoing theme.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce her as fresh information, but she has been the center of the chapter throughout.

prompt.context_jp: 「お隣ってことは これからも 気軽に情報交換できますね」
prompt.prompt_jp: お隣ってこと___、これからも気軽に情報交換できますね。

feedback.correct_en: 「〜ということは」is a set topicalizing phrase that frames a conclusion drawn from the given situation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「ということが」sounds ungrammatical here; this frame always uses は to introduce the premise.

contrast_examples.jp: 隣人ということは、よく会いますね。
contrast_examples.en: Since we're neighbors, we'll see each other often.

prompt.context_jp: 軽口の応酬が一段落したところで、支店長の古藤が資料を掲げて空気を切り替えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 軽口の応酬が一段落したところで、支店長の古藤___資料を掲げて空気を切り替えた。

feedback.correct_en: Kotō is newly introduced as the agent of this action within the scene; が marks this introduction of the active subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply Kotō had already been established as the topic, but the narrative is shifting focus to him as a new actor.

contrast_examples.en: The section chief stood up. (new actor)
The section chief is always late. (topic/general)

prompt.context_jp: 「何事も タイミングと勢いが大切です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 何事も、タイミングと勢い___大切です。

feedback.correct_en: This is an exhaustive-listing が: 'what matters (specifically) is timing and momentum.' It identifies the key factors.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would just introduce timing as a topic, losing the emphatic 'these are the crucial things' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 大事なのは努力が一番だ。
contrast_examples.en: What's important is effort above all. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 「馬場さん 結婚指輪してた」
prompt.prompt_jp: 馬場さん___結婚指輪してた。

feedback.correct_en: Baba-san is the topic Kaoru is commenting on — 'as for Baba-san, he was wearing a wedding ring.' This is topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly stress 'it was Baba-san (not someone else) who was wearing it,' which isn't the point.

contrast_examples.jp: 馬場さんは結婚してる。

prompt.context_jp: 「最大のミステリーは そこよね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 最大のミステリー___そこよね。

feedback.correct_en: 'The biggest mystery' is the topic being commented on, with そこ as the predicate — は presents it as the known theme.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would try to identify 最大のミステリー as new/exhaustive information, but the natural reading is topic-comment.

prompt.context_jp: 「結婚は タイミングと勢いです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 結婚___タイミングと勢いです。

feedback.correct_en: Baba is making a general statement about marriage as a concept — 'as for marriage, it's timing and momentum.' This is textbook topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read as 'it is marriage (specifically) that is timing and momentum,' which doesn't fit this maxim-style pronouncement.

prompt.context_jp: 「俺は いずれ区画整理され そこに総合病院が建つと思ってる」
prompt.prompt_jp: そこに総合病院___建つと思ってる。

feedback.correct_en: The general hospital is being introduced into the scene as new information — が marks this fresh element coming into existence.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presume the hospital was already a known topic, but Kotō is predicting its new arrival.

contrast_examples.en: A building will be built here. (new)

prompt.context_jp: 「新設される病院については まだ ほとんど情報がない」
prompt.prompt_jp: 新設される病院について___、まだほとんど情報がない。

feedback.correct_en: 「〜については」is the standard topic-framing structure: 'regarding the new hospital...' Only は fits after について to introduce the topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: 「についてが」is ungrammatical; this frame requires は to set up what the following comment is about.

contrast_examples.jp: その件については後で話そう。
contrast_examples.en: As for that matter, let's talk later.

prompt.context_jp: 懇親会という言葉に含まれた微妙な熱を、瀬川は敏感に嗅ぎ取っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 懇親会という言葉に含まれた微妙な熱を、瀬川___敏感に嗅ぎ取っていた。

feedback.correct_en: Segawa is already established in the scene and functions as the topic doing the sensing. は marks him as the ongoing theme.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark him as new or exhaustively specified, but he is a known participant here.

prompt.context_jp: この距離感こそが、ライバル会社の男が隣に住む厄介さのすべてだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: この距離感こそ___、ライバル会社の男が隣に住む厄介さのすべてだった。

feedback.correct_en: こそ pairs with が for emphatic exhaustive identification: 'this very sense of distance is precisely the whole problem.'
feedback.incorrect_en: こそは is uncommon and wouldn't carry the identifying 'that's exactly it' emphasis.

prompt.context_jp: 「私 このままだと タイミング 逃しそうです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私、このままだとタイミング___逃しそうです。

feedback.correct_en: 逃す is a transitive verb taking a direct object, so タイミングを逃す ('miss the timing') is the natural collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: が with 逃す would sound ungrammatical — the timing is being acted upon, not the actor.

prompt.context_jp: 「ハァ～ 何だか いろんなことが すべて うまくいくような気がする」
prompt.prompt_jp: 何だか いろんなことが すべて ___ような気がする。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the expression Mei uses to express that things seem to be going well.

feedback.correct_en: うまくいく is the set phrase for 'things going well / working out smoothly.'
feedback.incorrect_en: うまくなる means 'to become skilled,' and よくやる means 'to do well / do a lot,' neither of which fit 'things going smoothly.'

prompt.context_jp: メイは咄嗟に頬を引きつらせながら、余裕を装った笑みを作り直した。
prompt.prompt_jp: メイは咄嗟に頬を引きつらせながら、余裕を___笑みを作り直した。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that means she 'faked' composure.

feedback.correct_en: 装う means 'to feign / put on an air of,' perfect for pretending to be composed.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見つける ('find') and 失う ('lose') don't collocate with 余裕 to express pretending.

prompt.context_jp: この場を無事に切り抜けるには、もうひとつ嘘を重ねるしかない。
prompt.prompt_jp: この場を無事に___には、もうひとつ嘘を重ねるしかない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'to get through / escape this situation.'

feedback.correct_en: 切り抜ける means 'to get through / navigate out of a tough situation,' matching the context of escaping an awkward moment.
feedback.incorrect_en: 切り捨てる means 'to cut off / discard,' and 切り替える means 'to switch over,' neither of which fit.

prompt.context_jp: 嘘には嘘を重ねるほど、辻褄のためだけに小道具が増えていく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 嘘には嘘を___ほど、辻褄のためだけに小道具が増えていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb for 'piling lies on top of lies.'

feedback.correct_en: 嘘を重ねる is the idiomatic collocation for stacking/piling lies.
feedback.incorrect_en: 並べる means 'line up' and 広げる means 'spread out'; neither captures the layering sense.

prompt.context_jp: 「田所さん お隣同士というのは 秘密にしませんか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: お隣同士というのは ___しませんか？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word for 'keep it a secret.'

feedback.correct_en: 秘密にする ('to make it a secret') is the correct collocation with しませんか.
feedback.incorrect_en: 内緒で and 隠れて are adverbial forms and don't combine with しませんか as a predicate.

contrast_examples.jp: この話は秘密にしよう。

prompt.context_jp: 「何としても最初に うちの製品を採用してもらいたい」
prompt.prompt_jp: 何としても最初に うちの製品を___もらいたい。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb for 'have them adopt (our product).'

feedback.correct_en: 採用する is the business term for 'adopt / select (a product, proposal, person).'
feedback.incorrect_en: 採集 means 'collect specimens' and 採点 means 'grade/score'; neither fits a product being chosen by a hospital.

prompt.context_jp: 「くれぐれも内密にお願いします 特にアーノルドには」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___内密にお願いします。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the adverb meaning 'by all means / do take care to.'

feedback.correct_en: くれぐれも emphasizes a sincere request: 'please be sure to...' It fits formal requests to keep something confidential.
feedback.incorrect_en: いよいよ means 'at last' and そろそろ means 'soon / about time'; neither fits a plea for discretion.

contrast_examples.jp: くれぐれもお気をつけて。

prompt.context_jp: 「今の自分の生活を 1ミリも変えなくていい人！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 今の自分の生活を 1ミリ___変えなくていい人！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that goes with a negative predicate meaning 'not even.'

feedback.correct_en: The 'X も + negative' pattern means 'not even X' — here 'not even a millimeter.'
feedback.incorrect_en: は and が don't produce the emphatic 'not even' reading needed here.

contrast_examples.en: I don't have even one yen.

prompt.context_jp: 「承知しました」
prompt.prompt_jp: メイのお願いに対して、ナギサは「___」と答えた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the most appropriate polite acknowledgement Nagisa (a professional housekeeper) would use.

feedback.correct_en: 承知しました is the proper deferential response for a service professional accepting a client's request.
feedback.incorrect_en: 了解です is casual-business and inappropriate from a professional to a client; わかったよ is plain casual speech.

prompt.context_jp: Nagisa greets Mei formally as they begin the housekeeping contract.
prompt.prompt_en: Which greeting sounds most natural for a professional housekeeper starting a new contract?

choices.text: 本日より お世話になります よろしくお願いします
今日から 世話します よろしく
今日から お世話します よろしくね

feedback.correct_en: お世話になります is the formulaic humble greeting when entering someone's service; this phrasing fits a business introduction.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses plain 世話します (the server shouldn't 'take care of' as a plain verb to a client); C uses お世話します but the casual よろしくね is inappropriate for a first contract meeting.

contrast_examples.en: I'll be in your care. (said by the one entering the relationship)
I'll take care of you. (sounds patronizing to say to a client)

prompt.context_jp: Mei is scrambling to explain why she isn't using the bicycle she claimed to have.
prompt.prompt_en: Which excuse sounds most natural in casual spoken Japanese?

choices.text: 今 タイヤが パンクしてて
今 タイヤを パンクされて
今 タイヤに パンクして

feedback.correct_en: パンクする takes the tire as the subject with が: タイヤがパンクする ('the tire goes flat'). The て-form connects to context.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses a passive that doesn't fit this intransitive event; C misuses に where が is required.

contrast_examples.jp: 自転車のタイヤがパンクした。

contrast_examples.en: A hole opened in the tire.

prompt.context_jp: Mei texts Nagisa asking him to prepare a midnight snack.
prompt.prompt_en: Which request is most natural and appropriately polite to a service professional?

choices.text: 少しジャンクかつヘルシーな夜食を ご用意いただけますか？
少しジャンクかつヘルシーな夜食を 用意してくれる？
少しジャンクかつヘルシーな夜食を 用意しなさい

feedback.correct_en: ご用意いただけますか is a polite humble request suitable from a client to a hired housekeeper, consistent with Mei's messaging tone.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is too casual for the client-service register Mei uses with Nagisa; C is a command that would be rude to a professional.

contrast_examples.jp: ご確認いただけますか。
contrast_examples.en: Could I have you confirm this?

prompt.context_jp: Mei jokingly asks Nagisa to deny that she'll miss her chance to marry.
prompt.prompt_en: Which response by Nagisa most naturally gives the gentle reassurance Mei is fishing for?

choices.text: あっ そんなことないですよ
あっ そんなことありません
あっ そのことはないです

feedback.correct_en: そんなことないですよ is the natural soft denial/reassurance phrase in conversation, with よ adding warmth.
feedback.incorrect_en: B (そんなことありません) is more clipped/formal and less reassuring; C (そのこと) refers to a specific prior thing and sounds odd as a denial.

contrast_examples.jp: そんなことありません。
